minutes.headline: COA forms a subcommittee to push the Select Board for mail-in ballots for homebound seniors
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging board, meeting without its director or scribe present, agreed to form a subcommittee to petition the Select Board for mail-in balloting for homebound seniors, revisited a lapsed friendly-visit/friendly-call program for isolated seniors, and worked through confusion over multiple senior-center donation funds (the COA gift fund versus the Eagle House Supporters). It also elected its officers for the coming year, added two new honorary members, and heard reports on staffing, facilities, and upcoming senior programs, with several policy questions (gift fund handling, veterans-breakfast fees, bylaws) left open for a future meeting.

votes.motion: Form a subcommittee to explore mail-in/absentee voting facilitation with the Select Board and town clerk, and report back with a draft letter
Seek town manager authorization to place the COA orientation packet, including policies and procedures, on the town website
Approve the officer slate (chair and vice chair) for the new year
Amend the honorary-member policy to allow, at the Council's discretion, people who were not previously COA members to become honorary members
Nominate Susan Doherty as an honorary member of the Council on Aging

budget_items.topic: Charlene Adams gift to the Eagle House / COA fund
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member noted the contribution from the Adams family was substantial, prompting questions about which fund it went to and what policy governs such gifts.
A board member said she thought this amount was currently in the COA gift fund, but another member said she did not know, and the director was not present to confirm.

budget_items.topic: Large donor gift to Eagle House Supporters
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member described a recent large gift where the donor initially wanted to stay anonymous, then agreed to be acknowledged so it might inspire others to give.

Veterans attending the breakfast eat free while their caregivers are charged a fee; the amount was stated inconsistently in the discussion, and the fee was described as covering costs the Highlands sponsorship does not fully cover.
The outgoing volunteer offered stamps and a small cash contribution to the new volunteer taking over the card-sending program, since cards are expensive.
The trips coordinator explained that funds raised go partly to the director each fiscal year and partly back into running trips, with prices kept low so seniors are not overcharged.
The chair said the financial report provided did not include the level of detail expected, such as the COA account and formula grant balances, and asked that better detail be provided next time.

A board member described a difficult personal experience re-quoting car and home insurance amid significant rate increases and asked whether the board should offer a seminar to help seniors navigate insurance comparisons.

decisions.decision: Pursue a publicity push (newsletter, cable/PACK crawl, Meals on Wheels flyers) to identify isolated seniors for a revived friendly-visit/friendly-call program, without a formal vote.
Table the question of COA gift fund policy and Eagle House Supporters fund separation until the director can provide input at a future meeting.
Keep the gift fund/donor policy question on the agenda for the next meeting pending clarification from the director.
Board members agreed they should be informed going forward whenever an operational policy (such as the veterans breakfast fee) changes.
Hold off submitting the COA bylaws until vague provisions conflicting with the Mass Council on Aging model are resolved, and identify the current bylaw committee.
Move the honorary-member recognition luncheon from August to September due to a member's scheduled knee surgery.
Add a caregiver support session update as a standing placeholder on the next meeting's agenda.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging board voted to form a subcommittee to petition the Select Board and town clerk for mail-in ballots for homebound seniors.
The board elected its chair and vice chair for the coming year.
The board amended its honorary-member policy and nominated a new honorary member, its third.
A question over whether a large donation belongs to the COA gift fund or the separate Eagle House Supporters fund was tabled until the director can weigh in.
The chair said the financial report given to the board lacked the account and grant-balance detail requested and asked for more detail next time.

why_it_matters: A subcommittee pushing for mail-in ballots for homebound seniors could affect how those residents vote in future town elections, pending Select Board and town clerk action.
Unresolved confusion between the COA gift fund and the Eagle House Supporters fund means donors and the board itself are currently unclear which fund a gift lands in and what policy governs it.
A caregiver fee at the veterans breakfast was changed without the board being informed, which the board flagged as a gap in oversight of day-to-day COA policy changes going forward.
